property_summary: After calling owned(), the owner state variable remains unchanged from its value before the call.
After a call to owned(), the owner remains the same as before the call
After calling owned(), the owner must be the same as the value set by the last successful transferOwnership call.
After calling owned(), the owner should not be the zero address if it was previously a non-zero address.
After calling owned(), the owner must be the address that was last set by a successful transferOwnership call (i.e., not the zero address unless explicitly set to zero).
The owner address is unchanged after calling owned()
Calling owned() does not revert when msg.sender is the owner.
If owned() is called by the owner, it does not revert; if called by a non-owner, it reverts.
After calling owned(), the owner address stored in the contract is the same as msg.sender if the call succeeded, or unchanged if the call reverted.
Calling owned() with any sender should never revert.
After calling owned(), the owner is always the caller.
After calling owned() by a caller that is not the owner, the owner address remains unchanged.
Only the current owner can successfully call owned() without reverting.
After calling owned(), the owner state variable remains unchanged.
After a call to owned() by any address, the caller cannot become the new owner via transferOwnership without authorization.
